name: Rust edition
meaning: A selected set of compatible Rust language rules, independent of the compiler release number.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: numeric type
meaning: A type defining how numbers are represented and which values and operations are supported.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: Unicode scalar value
meaning: A Unicode code point excluding surrogate code points; the kind of value represented by Rust char.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: tuple destructuring
meaning: Binding tuple elements to names according to their positions.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: loop expression
meaning: A loop that can yield a result through break with a value.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: tail expression
meaning: The final expression of a Rust block whose value becomes the block’s result.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: Rust ownership
meaning: Responsibility for a value and its eventual release, enforced through Rust’s rules.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: move
meaning: Transferring ownership so the previous binding cannot keep using the moved value.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: clone
meaning: An explicit type-defined operation for creating another value, not necessarily a deep copy for every type.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: shared borrow
meaning: A reference allowing shared read access while another binding remains the owner.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: mutable borrow
meaning: An exclusive reference permitting mutation while its access remains active.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: borrow lifetime
meaning: The region during which a reference must remain valid and its borrowing restrictions apply.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: Rust vector
meaning: An owned growable sequence whose initialized element count is distinct from its capacity.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: slice
meaning: A contiguous sequence of elements, often accessed through a borrowed reference such as &[T].
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: Option
meaning: An enum representing either a present Some value or explicit None absence.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: question-mark propagation
meaning: Unwrapping success or returning a compatible failure to the caller.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: field ownership
meaning: Ownership rules apply independently to owned fields inside a struct.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: mutable receiver
meaning: A method receiver borrowing exclusive mutable access to its object.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: enum payload
meaning: Data carried by a particular enum variant.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: match guard
meaning: An additional Boolean condition on a match arm.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: trait
meaning: A named behavior contract implemented by types.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: derived trait
meaning: A compiler-generated trait implementation supported by a type’s fields.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: generic type
meaning: A type declaration parameterized by one or more type arguments.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: trait object
meaning: A dynamically dispatched value viewed through a compatible trait, here by borrowing.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: lifetime relationship
meaning: A contract relating how long borrowed inputs and outputs may be used.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: dangling-reference prevention
meaning: Rejecting references whose owners cannot remain alive for the required use.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: lazy iterator
meaning: A stateful producer whose adapters do work as items are requested.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: closure capture
meaning: Access to a variable from the environment of an anonymous function.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: move closure
meaning: A closure capturing its environment by value, with moves for non-Copy captures.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: collect destination
meaning: The result type that determines how iterator items are gathered.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: UTF-8 boundary
meaning: A byte position between complete Unicode scalar encodings rather than inside one.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: entry API
meaning: Access to an existing map value or an insertion point for a missing key.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: HashSet
meaning: A hash-based collection of unique values without stable iteration order.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: module visibility
meaning: Rules controlling which module paths can access an item.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: path dependency
meaning: A Cargo dependency resolved from a supplied local directory.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: Integration test
meaning: A test compiled as an external consumer of a library’s public interface.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: Domain error
meaning: A typed failure representing a violated application rule, with intentionally chosen context.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: Box ownership
meaning: Unique ownership of a heap allocation through an owning pointer with a finite-sized representation.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: Reference-counted ownership
meaning: Keeping an allocation alive while one or more strong owning pointers refer to it.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: Runtime borrow guard
meaning: A value whose lifetime represents a currently active RefCell borrow.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: Atomic shared ownership
meaning: Reference-counted ownership with thread-safe count updates, subject to the payload’s thread-safety bounds.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: Mutex guard
meaning: An owned lock token that provides protected access and releases the lock when dropped.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: Join handle
meaning: A handle used to wait for a thread and observe its returned value or panic.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: Sender lifetime
meaning: The period during which sender handles can still produce messages; receiver iteration ends only after all senders are gone and queued values drained.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: Send and Sync
meaning: Marker traits for safe transfer of ownership and safe sharing of references across threads, respectively.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: Error propagation
meaning: Returning a failure to the caller rather than silently substituting a successful-looking value.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: Bounded line parsing
meaning: Reading and validating lines under explicit input-size, line-count and value limits.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: Path value
meaning: A platform-aware representation of a filesystem location, not proof that the location exists.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: Argument validation
meaning: Checking the number and meaning of command-line values before relying on them.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: Validation policy
meaning: The explicitly chosen normalization, syntax and domain rules determining which inputs are accepted.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: Display contract
meaning: User-facing formatting through a borrowed Formatter with a returned formatting Result.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: Lazy future
meaning: A value describing asynchronous work whose body does not progress until driven by polling.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: Bounded future poll
meaning: A deliberately limited poll of a known-ready future, not a runtime for arbitrary asynchronous work.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: Macro evaluation count
meaning: The number of times an expanded macro causes a captured expression to execute.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: Unsafe contract
meaning: A safety obligation that must be upheld for an operation requiring unsafe, not a waiver of Rust’s validity rules.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.

name: Bounded validation pipeline
meaning: A finite sequence of parsing, domain filtering and capped collection with an explicit rejection policy.
context: Rust language and standard-library semantics; edition2024 core.
